classification.difficultyReason: Combine special-figure properties, angle sums and simple equations across six compound figures.

content.prompt: Work out the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle between marked parallel horizontal lines; upper exterior sector 62°, interior labels e, f, g.
spec.mathematics: Matching single ticks on the sloping sides and matching single parallel arrows.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles give $e=62^\circ$. The marked equal sides make the triangle isosceles, so $f=e=62^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}g+62+62&=180\\g+124&=180\\g&=56^\circ\end{align*}$$
The interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.

spec.description: Rectangle with four right-angle squares and two internal segments sharing a point on the left side.
spec.mathematics: 158° at the top-side intersection and 76° at bottom right; unknowns w, x, y.

answer.worked:
At the bottom-right right angle:
$$\begin{align*}x+76&=90\\x&=14^\circ\end{align*}$$
In the lower triangle:
$$\begin{align*}y+90+14&=180\\y+104&=180\\y&=76^\circ\end{align*}$$
The acute angle where the upper segment meets the top side is $180^\circ-158^\circ=22^\circ$. The top and bottom sides of the rectangle are parallel, so the upper segment makes $22^\circ$ with a horizontal line through the left-side point. Thus
$$\begin{align*}w&=22+14\\w&=36^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Left quadrilateral and right triangle share a segment; the top edge is straight through the shared vertex.
spec.mathematics: Quadrilateral givens 109°, 58°, 124°; triangle given 21°; unknowns w, x, y.

answer.worked:
The interior angles of the left quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}w+109+58+124&=360\\w+291&=360\\w&=69^\circ\end{align*}$$
The top edge is a straight line.
$$\begin{align*}x+69&=180\\x&=111^\circ\end{align*}$$
The interior angles of the right triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}y+111+21&=180\\y+132&=180\\y&=48^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram with two distinct parallel-marker families and a lower-left internal triangle.
spec.mathematics: Givens 130° and 115°; unknowns w, x, y.

answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line give
$$\begin{align*}w+130&=180\\w&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles between the marked parallel sides give
$$\begin{align*}x+115&=180\\x&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$
In the lower-left triangle:
$$\begin{align*}y+50+65&=180\\y+115&=180\\y&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Concave quadrilateral with w in the reflex interior region and y outside the extended lower-right side.
spec.mathematics: Givens 41°, 132° and 55°; 132° is the smaller outside angle at the concave vertex.

answer.worked:
Angles around the concave vertex sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}w+132&=360\\w&=228^\circ\end{align*}$$
Use the reflex interior angle in the quadrilateral angle sum.
$$\begin{align*}x+41+228+55&=360\\x+324&=360\\x&=36^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line give
$$\begin{align*}y+55&=180\\y&=125^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Trapezium with a marked horizontal parallel pair and the right side extended below the lower vertex.
spec.mathematics: Left angles w and 66°; right angles 3x and x; exterior angle y.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles between the parallel sides sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}3x+x&=180\\4x&=180\\x&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
On the left side:
$$\begin{align*}w+66&=180\\w&=114^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line give
$$\begin{align*}y+45&=180\\y&=135^\circ\end{align*}$$
